question.text: How many storms will the UK–Ireland–Netherlands storm-naming group have named by the end of 28 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: Resolves to the number of distinct names from the 2026/27 west-group list (Austen, Boelo, Chloe, Dano, Evelyn, Finn, Gwendolyn, Heather, Ivy, Jade, Kilian, Laoise, Miriam, Nicola, Olaf, Phelim, Ruban, Shaun, Theo, Vesna, Wende) that have been assigned to a storm with a "Date named" on or before 28 November 2026, as shown in the named-storm table at the Met Office UK Storm Centre: https://weather.metoffice.gov.uk/warnings-and-advice/uk-storm-centre. For example, a resolution of 3 means a third name had been announced by that date; a resolution of 2 means no third storm had been named. As of 13 November 2026 the table lists two storms — Austen (named 20 October 2026) and Boelo (named 22 October 2026) — so 2 is the current count. Dates on the Met Office table are UK local calendar dates (GMT in November, equivalent to UTC); if the table is unavailable or not yet updated, the storm-names page of Met Éireann (https://www.met.ie/forecasts/storm-names) or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) may be used instead. Each name counts once, and a name is credited on the date it was announced, not the date the storm affected land.
question.fine_print: Only names from the 2026/27 west-group list count; a storm named by another European naming group (for example the French/Spanish/Portuguese or northern groups) does not count even if it affects the UK, Ireland or the Netherlands.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** The outcome cannot go below 2. Blocking could persist through 28 November, or an Atlantic low could arrive but stay below the amber-warning threshold (as happened after Boelo). Either way the count stays at 2.
- **High:** The pattern flips quickly around 24 November to a strong jet stream. Two deep lows follow, for example one Met Éireann names for Ireland and one KNMI names for the Netherlands, taking the count to 4.
